title: LOS waypoint path following at the TVC limit
description:
3D line-of-sight (lookahead) guidance through a staggered waypoint zig-zag (East, then North, then back West) during the powered ascent. Guidance steers the velocity vector toward a point 150 m ahead on the active segment; the flight computer turns that into an angle-of-attack command for the gain-scheduled attitude PID, using the KF navigation estimate (GPS + baro + IMU, Gaussian noise).

The vehicle constraint drives the design: TVC only has authority while the motor burns (until 3.97 s), and the AoA it can hold against the fins shrinks from ~29 deg at rail exit to <1 deg at the end of the boost. The 'Authority envelope' variant maps how big a lateral jog is flyable at each altitude. The aggressive path is placed at that edge, and the 'Beyond' variant shows a jog the vehicle cannot fly. Cross-track metrics are over the guided window; after TVC ends the rocket coasts ballistically to apogee.

variants.notes: Aggressive zig-zag placed at the edge of the envelope (see the 'Authority envelope' variant): East jog (8.5 deg path turn) by 40 m AGL, North jog (9.5 deg) by 100 m, back West (4.3 deg) by 180 m, then a NNW climb-out, all within the first ~2.1 s of the 3.97 s guided window. LOS guidance (lookahead 150 m, k = 1.5, switching radius 40 m) turns the velocity vector toward the lookahead point. Gravity-compensated lateral-acceleration commands become an AoA command, clipped to 60 % of what the gimbal can hold. From ~1.4 s on, the AoA command rides that clip and the gimbal works close to 5 deg to hold the trim AoA against the fins' restoring moment. The gentle doc path (one inclined line) is overlaid as a baseline.

variants.notes: Same zig-zag with 10 m/s wind from the West (1/7 shear), 3 m/s turbulence, 4 m/s 1-cos side gust at 1.5 s, 0.25 deg thrust misalignment per axis. The three jog waypoints are still passed within ~10 m, but the gimbal now spends over a third of the guided window pinned at 5 deg fighting the weathercock moment. On the climb-out (after ~2 s, when the AoA clip is down to 1-3 deg) nothing is left to reject the wind drift, so the cross-track error grows to ~40 m by TVC end (RMS ~18 m vs ~8 m in calm air). The same disturbance with the wind from the East instead happens to push the vehicle along the West leg (see metrics: RMS ~6 m). Near the authority limit, wind direction matters more than tuning.

variants.notes: Deliberately infeasible: the same zig-zag plus a 20 m East jog between 300 and 450 m AGL (t ~ 2.6-3.2 s, qbar > 30 kPa). The guidance asks for it, but the AoA command is pinned at the authority clip (~1-1.5 deg) and the rocket barely moves: the jog waypoint is missed by ~16 m and the cross-track error grows to ~26 m by the time TVC ends. A jog of the same size flown below 100 m is easy (see the first variant). This is where TVC authority runs out, not a tuning problem.

tables.title: Envelope sweep: single lateral jog (0,0,0) -> rail line at h -> +J North over 200 m of climb -> straight

variants.notes: How big a lateral jog can the TVC fly, and how late? Each run is a single jog: follow the rail line to altitude h, then move J m North over the next 200 m of climb, then continue straight. Starting at 30 m AGL (t ~0.9 s) the rocket achieves ~80 % of even a 60 m jog; starting at 100 m (t ~1.5 s) only ~50 % of a 15 m jog; by 200 m (t ~2.1 s) <= 21 %; and above 300 m (t > 2.6 s, qbar > 30 kPa) < 10 %: the AoA the gimbal can hold against the fins (alpha_hold) has collapsed to 1-3 deg, and the climb leaves less than 1.5 s of TVC time. Lateral velocity built early also cannot be removed later, so every jog in a zig-zag must be finished, and the climb-out direction matched, by ~2 s. This sweep set the waypoints of the aggressive path.
